verified.exploit_entry_point: Real embedded Tomcat connectors on ephemeral loopback ports with TLS enabled and several SSLHostConfigs (default without client authentication, strict.example.com requiring a client certificate, a wildcard configuration). The hidden tests open real SSLSockets with an explicit TLS host name and a real client certificate, send HTTP/1.1 requests or an HTTP/2 preface + HEADERS frame, and assert a client error with no servlet invocation (a static counter in the served application). A second I/O implementation (NIO2), an adapter that fixes the served name, and an HTTP/2 ALPN connector are exercised through the same real entry points.

java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/AbstractEndpoint.java:737 (checkSni policy: resolved-config comparison and case-insensitive protocol host; absent at pinned)

traps.shape: the published fix's site: the TLS host negotiated for the connection must resolve to the same TLS configuration as the host the request is served under; a request that names another host is a client error with no application invocation
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the request names a host and the TLS connection already selected a configuration, so a client that sends a different name looks like an ordinary virtual-host request
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (GHSA-fpj8-gq4v-p354); the two transports and the second I/O implementation are the published fix's own scope

traps.shape: the same protected outcome over the second request-processing front end: an HTTP/2 request whose authority names another virtual host
traps.reason_to_dismiss: HTTP/2 is a separate binary front end with its own header handling; a fix written against the HTTP/1.1 parser looks complete and the second implementation is easy to miss
traps.realistic_because: published fix site: the published fix changes both front ends

traps.shape: a connection that sent no TLS host name still has a TLS configuration in force (the default one); a request naming a host with a different configuration must be refused, while a request that resolves to the default configuration must be served
traps.reason_to_dismiss: with no TLS name there is nothing to compare, so treating the request as unconstrained looks reasonable; rejecting it instead breaks ordinary clients
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream semantics: getSSLHostConfig(null) returns the default configuration and the mapping falls back to the default host

traps.shape: the request host differs from the TLS host only in case: the configuration lookup is case-sensitive while the virtual-host mapping is case-insensitive, so a name-spelling difference makes the guard see the default configuration
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the first fix already compares names case-insensitively, so the case dimension looks handled; the resolved-configuration fallback is the path that still uses the unnormalised name
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (GHSA-8mc5-53m5-3qj2, the incomplete-fix advisory): the second fix lower-cases the protocol host name before the configuration lookup

traps.shape: the connector serves the request under a name different from the one the request carries; the guard on the request name passes while the actually-served virtual host has a different TLS configuration
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the connector's served name is an administrator setting applied after the request is parsed, and the request name still matches the TLS name, so the deployment looks consistent
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the served name is resolved after the request-level checks in both published fix commits
